data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kutah’, meaning a fort, hill or fortress. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is often referred to as Kota or Kotaraja, meaning the king of the fort. The name Kota carries the meaning “Fort, Hill, Fortress” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kota usually hope their child will grow to embody fort, hill, fortress and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kota belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fort, Hill, Fortress.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kota total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kota holds historical and cultural significance as it is derived from the ancient term 'kutah' in Sanskrit, which refers to a stronghold, citadel or fortress. In India, the name Kota has been associated with various cities, towns and empires due to its significance as a place of strength and protection. The cities of Kota in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh are notable examples of this ancient meaning.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is often referred to as Kota or Kotaraja. This divine name signifies his role as the supreme protector, the king of all gods. Lord Shiva is revered as the destroyer of negative energies and the giver of peace and tranquility. By invoking the name Kota, oneconnects with the divine aspect of strength, protection, and the power to destroy inner negativity. This spiritual significance adds a profound layer of meaning to the name Kota, extending beyond its historical and cultural significance.
